one_line: Proximity-based voice chat that connects players' browsers to an external Node/WebRTC server so nearby characters hear each other talk, with optional global and ghost channels.
player_facing_mechanics: Join voice chat with the default browser via the ProxChat 'Join' verb
Join using an external URL (link/QR) via the 'Join with URL' verb for browsers that fail to auto-open
See a floating voice/speaker overlay icon above a mob while it is speaking
Hear only players within proximity on the same Z-level/room
Be moved to non-proximity global channels (lobby/round-end) where everyone can hear everyone
Become automatically silenced/muted from proximity when knocked out, deaf, mute, or miming
Be placed in a ghost channel when dead and returned to normal voice room when revived
Leave voice chat with the 'Leave' verb
Read in-client help/troubleshooting via the 'Help' verb
Admins can restart voice chat (disconnecting everyone)
Admins can stop voice chat entirely
type_paths: /mob (verbs join_vc, join_with_url, help_voicechat, mute_self, deafen, leave)
tg_systems_used: signals and signal handlers (COMSIG_TOPIC, COMSIG_MOB_LOGOUT, COMSIG_QDELETING, COMSIG_LIVING_DEATH, COMSIG_LIVING_REVIVE, SIGNAL_ADDTRAIT/REMOVETRAIT)
data_only_parts: Room constants/definitions (ROOM_NONE, ROOM_INVALID, ROOM_GHOST, ROOM_GLOBAL_LOBBY) and GLOB.rooms_proximity / GLOB.rooms_global room lists
mob voice variable defaults (voice_chat_room, voice_icon_state) and the voice_overlay.dmi icon reference
The static help HTML text in help_voicechat
Trait-to-room mapping rules (which traits silence a player)
logic_parts: Subsystem lifecycle: Initialize, fire() location broadcasting loop, Shutdown, restart
Room membership management (add_rooms, remove_rooms, clear_userCode, move_userCode_to_room)
Client/userCode/session registration and mapping (open_vc, generate_userCode, confirm_userCode, link_userCode_client, disconnect)
Per-mob signal registration and condition evaluation (register_mob_signals, on_mob_changed, check_mob_conditions, clear_from_room, add_to_room, on_mob_death/revive)
Overlay toggling (toggle_voice_overlay) driven by voice-activity callbacks
JSON packet encoding/sanitization and topic/route dispatch (send_json, send_locations, handle_topic)
Round-end relocation of all clients to the global lobby room
byond_specific: External process launch via shell('node ... &') and world.process / world.port / world.internet_address
call_ext to a native BYOND socket library (voicechat/pipes/unix/byondsocket: byond:Echo, byond:SendJSON) - the Node <-> BYOND bridge
Inbound redirects/traffic via a Topic handler (handle_topic) restricted to addr 127.0.0.1
Client output via << browse(), browse_rsc() asset delivery, link(), window= targeting
Client-only web glue: window.location origin capture, WebRTC in the player's browser, socket.io client JS
world.system_type / OS-specific shell commands (kill vs taskkill /F /PID) to stop the node process
port_notes: The BYOND side is thin glue: it tracks player positions/rooms and forwards JSON over a native socket library to an out-of-process Node/WebRTC relay that does the actual audio; almost nothing here maps to SS14 gameplay prototypes, so this is infrastructure, not content. An SS14 port would replace the subsystem with an ECS system that maintains per-session entities/components (position, session id, room) and raises events on mob state changes (KO/deaf/mute/death) plus a round-end rule, using SS14's existing signal/CVars/DoAfter-free patterns, and swap the browse/call_ext bridge for SS14's own voice server (RobustToolbox already ships a WebRTC voice server) with components for microphone/mute state. Key human decisions: reuse SS14's built-in voice chat versus re-implement this Node relay; how proximity is computed in the grid/space world (Z-level + tile radius vs SS14 maps); how to model global/ghost/lobby channels as rule or system state; and how admin restart/stop and per-player mute are exposed through SS14 admin tools rather than BYOND verbs.
